meta.titre: Developing a New System: life cycle, fact finding, design and changeover

sections.contenu_markdown: A secondary school in Bafoussam records fees in exercise books, and the bursar cannot say quickly who still owes money. Before anyone buys a computer, someone must find out how fees are collected today, what goes wrong, and what a better system must do. That work belongs to the systems analyst, and examination questions ask you to put the stages in order, to name ways of finding facts, to describe what is produced at each stage, and to choose a safe way of bringing the new system into use.

items: A system is a set of parts (inputs, processes and outputs) that work together to reach a goal.
A user is a person who operates a system, and a stakeholder is anyone with an interest in it, such as managers, staff and customers.
A database stores structured data, and a program is a set of instructions that a computer follows.

sections.titre: The life cycle, fact finding and the design document
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The systems development life cycle (SDLC)
The SDLC is the ordered set of stages through which a computer system is planned, built, brought into use and kept useful. Books group the stages in slightly different ways, so follow the order and use the names in the question.

| Stage | Main work | What is produced |
|---|---|---|
| Planning and feasibility study | decide whether the project is worth doing; estimate cost and benefits (cost-benefit analysis) | feasibility report |
| Analysis | study the current system by fact finding; find problems and user requirements | requirements specification |
| Design | decide how the new system will meet the requirements | design document |
| Development | write or configure the software, build the database, buy equipment, test each part | working system |
| Testing | check that the whole system works and meets the requirements | test results |
| Installation | change over to the new system, train the users, convert data | system in use |
| Maintenance and review | correct faults, adapt and improve, then evaluate against the requirements | evaluation report |

A feasibility study looks at whether the project is technically possible, economically worthwhile, operationally acceptable to users, legal and achievable in the time available.

### Fact finding in the analysis stage
| Method | Advantage | Disadvantage |
|---|---|---|
| Interview | detailed answers and follow-up questions are possible | slow, and answers may be biased |
| Questionnaire | reaches many people cheaply, answers are easy to compare | some people do not reply and questions can be misread |
| Observation | shows what really happens | people may behave differently when watched; takes time |
| Document inspection | shows the forms, reports and data volumes in use | documents may be out of date and hide unwritten practices |

### The design document
Analysis decides **what** the system must do; design decides **how**. A design document normally contains the requirements being met, the hardware and software chosen, the data design (tables, fields, data types and validation rules), the input and output design (forms and reports), the process design (flowcharts, pseudocode or data flow diagrams), the user interface, the security measures and the test plan. Writing the program code belongs to the development stage, after the design has been approved.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to recommend or compare ways of replacing the old system.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
| Method | How it works | Advantage | Disadvantage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Direct | the old system stops and the new one starts at once | cheap and quick | high risk, nothing to fall back on |
| Parallel | both systems run together for a time | outputs can be compared, safe | double work and cost |
| Phased | the new system is introduced one part at a time | problems are limited to one part | slow, and old and new parts must work together |
| Pilot | the new system is first used in one branch or department | a small group finds the problems | other sites wait longer |

A recommendation must be justified from the scenario: a payroll or hospital system that cannot stop favours parallel running.

variantes.nom: Types of testing and test data
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how a new system or a validation rule is tested.
variantes.contenu_markdown: **Unit testing** checks each module alone, **integration testing** checks that the modules work together, **system testing** checks the whole system against the requirements, and **acceptance testing** is done by the users with real data before they accept the system. Test data are of three kinds: **normal** (valid), **extreme or boundary** (values at the limits of the valid range) and **erroneous** (invalid data that must be rejected). For an age field that accepts 18 to 65 inclusive, 30 is normal, 18 and 65 are boundary values, and 17, 66 and the text "abc" are rejected.

variantes.nom: Development approaches and types of maintenance
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to compare ways of organising development, or to name kinds of maintenance.
variantes.contenu_markdown: In the **waterfall** approach each stage is finished and approved before the next begins: it is easy to manage and document, but changes are hard once a stage is closed. In **prototyping** or iterative development a working model is built, shown to users and improved in cycles: users see progress early, but the final cost and time are harder to predict. Maintenance is **corrective** (fixing faults), **adaptive** (changing the system for new conditions such as a new law) or **perfective** (improving speed or adding features).

sections.enonce_markdown: A pharmacy in Garoua keeps its stock on index cards, and items often run out without anyone noticing. The owner has been quoted 2 400 000 FCFA for a computerised stock system which should save about 600 000 FCFA each year in lost sales and wasted time. (a) Name TWO fact-finding methods that the analyst should use and give a reason for each. [4 marks] (b) State what the analyst produces at the end of the analysis stage. [1 mark] (c) Calculate how many years the system takes to pay for itself and say what this tells the owner. [2 marks] (d) Recommend a method of changeover and justify it. [2 marks]

etapes.action: Read the command words and the marks.
etapes.justification: "Name ... and give a reason" needs a method and a reason; "calculate" needs working; "recommend" needs a justification tied to the pharmacy.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Nine marks: two methods with reasons, one product, one calculation with comment, one justified choice.

etapes.action: Choose fact-finding methods that fit this pharmacy.
etapes.justification: The staff know why items run out, and the cards show how stock is recorded now.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Interview the pharmacist and assistants; inspect the stock cards and order forms.

etapes.justification: Analysis ends by recording what the new system must do.
Payback period = cost divided by yearly saving.
Medicines are sold every day, so stock data must never be lost.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Parallel running for a short period, or phased introduction.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **(a)** An **interview** with the pharmacist and assistants gives detailed answers about why stock runs out, and the analyst can ask follow-up questions. **Document inspection** of the index cards and order forms shows exactly what data is recorded now and in what quantity. **(b)** A requirements specification. **(c)** $2\,400\,000 \div 600\,000 = 4$ years: the system pays for itself in **4 years**; the owner can decide whether this is acceptable, and should also count benefits that are hard to measure, such as customers who are no longer turned away. **(d)** **Parallel running**: the cards and the new system are used together for a few weeks, so that the stock figures can be compared and the pharmacy can fall back on the cards if the new system fails.

items.erreur_markdown: Describing the layout of forms and reports in the analysis stage.
items.pourquoi_faux: Analysis finds out what the system must do. Deciding how the screens, reports and files will look is design.
items.correction_markdown: Analysis: investigate, find problems, record requirements. Design: forms, reports, data structures, processes.

items.erreur_markdown: "Direct changeover is the safest because it is the quickest."
items.pourquoi_faux: Direct changeover is the riskiest: the old system is gone, so a fault in the new one stops the organisation.
items.correction_markdown: Parallel running is the safest because the old system is kept as a fall-back; direct changeover is cheap but risky.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing "interview, questionnaire, observation" with no more detail when asked to compare them.
items.pourquoi_faux: A comparison needs an advantage or a disadvantage of each method, ideally linked to the scenario.
items.correction_markdown: State what each method gives and one weakness, for example: questionnaires reach many people but some do not reply.

items.pourquoi_faux: Correcting faults is only one kind. The system is also adapted to changed conditions and improved.
items.correction_markdown: Maintenance is corrective, adaptive or perfective.

items.enonce_markdown: Name TWO fact-finding methods other than an interview and state ONE disadvantage of each.
items.solution_markdown:
Award a mark for each method and a mark for each matching disadvantage. Any two of:

- **Questionnaire**: some people do not return it, or they misunderstand a question.
- **Observation**: people may behave differently when they know they are watched, and it takes a long time.
- **Document inspection**: the documents may be out of date and do not show tasks that are done without paperwork.

**Two methods, each with one disadvantage.**

items.enonce_markdown: A cybercafe in Limbe is offered a booking system for 1 500 000 FCFA. It costs 150 000 FCFA each year to maintain and it saves 600 000 FCFA each year in staff time and lost bookings. (a) Calculate the net saving each year. (b) Calculate the payback period in years and months. (c) Name the stage of the life cycle in which this calculation is first done.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Net saving $= 600\,000 - 150\,000 = $ **450 000 FCFA per year**.

(b) Payback $= 1\,500\,000 \div 450\,000 = 3.33$ years. The fraction $0.33 \times 12 = 4$ months, so the payback period is **3 years 4 months**.

(c) The **planning and feasibility study** stage, where costs and benefits are compared to decide whether the project should go ahead.

items.enonce_markdown: A regional hospital will replace its computerised payroll system, which must produce correct salaries every month. (a) Recommend a method of changeover and justify it. (b) The new system has a field for the number of days worked in a month, which must accept whole numbers from 0 to 31. Give TWO items of normal data, TWO items of extreme data and TWO items of erroneous data for this field. (c) Explain why acceptance testing is done by the users and not only by the developers.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Parallel running**: the old and new payroll are run together for at least one pay period and the salaries produced are compared. If the new system gives a wrong figure, the old system still gives the correct payment, so no employee is paid wrongly. (Phased changeover, one department at a time, with a reason, is also acceptable.)

(b) Normal: 15 and 22. Extreme (boundary): 0 and 31. Erroneous: 32 and -1 (also 15.5 or the text "ten"), which the system must reject.

(c) The users know the real tasks and the real data and can judge whether the system does what they need. The developers test against the design, so they can miss a requirement that was misunderstood. Acceptance by the users confirms that the system is fit for its purpose before it is paid for and used.

items_markdown: The SDLC runs from planning and feasibility and analysis through design, development, testing and installation to maintenance and review.
Analysis finds what the system must do and produces a requirements specification; design decides how and produces the design document.
Fact-finding methods are interviews, questionnaires, observation and document inspection, and each has a strength and a weakness.
The cost of a project is first estimated in the planning and feasibility study, and payback period = cost divided by yearly net saving.
Changeover can be direct, parallel, phased or pilot; parallel is the safest and direct the riskiest.
Test data are normal, extreme (boundary) and erroneous, and maintenance is corrective, adaptive or perfective.
